sovereign-actor networking — keypair-as-PID, identity-addressed delivery, paid inboxes, spawn-as-funded-enrollment; near-term: decentralized identity networking
notes:
Triangle: self-certifying / rotatable / offline-verifiable — pick two. Actor end-state forces stable-handle+rotatable corner; indirection layer (chain registry or attestation CA) is non-optional. Raw hash(pubkey) addressing ruled out as destination.

CA reframed as SPKI/SDSI pattern: a key whose claims peers locally honor; hierarchy is emergent policy over flat keyspace. Repo already does this (wallet-derived issuer keys, invariant 1).

Money enters only where mutual distrust meets scarce resources. First real customer: paid inboxes (store-and-forward for offline actors). Payment-channel-to-mailbox is an unexplored gap (Nostr=altruism, DIDComm=punt, AO=on-chain gas per msg).

Spawn = ADR-0012 enrollment generalized: child-born keypair + parent attestation + parent funding. Supervision tree = funding tree on crypto clouds (lease lapse = crash).

Prior art map: Urbit/Ames (identity-addressed msgs, rotatable via Azimuth), Agoric/Spritely (ocap actors + currency — security model is capabilities not ACLs), AO/Arweave (inbox-on-chain, closest to full vision), Erlang (semantics; PID→keypair is the novel twist). Nebula multi-CA on one device key ≈ multi-network attachment today.

REVISED: actor model = stateful but volatile; mailboxes don't survive crashes (Erlang at-most-once, sender-side retry, supervisors restart from spec). Paid-inbox claim demoted: Fork A model-faithful sender-holds-queue (stateless, no payment) vs Fork B durable mailbox hosts (only if never-simultaneously-online parties exist). Test: who is the sender that can't hold its own queue?

Triage: Tier1 borrow (Noise, NAT/relay per ADR-0006, ADR-0012 ceremony, OTP supervision). Tier2 decide (identity handle=root dep; weak delivery semantics — Ames exactly-once regret; spawn payload; rendezvous). Tier3 hard: (A) hot-wallet custody on rented compute → allowances-not-balances, funding tree = blast radius; (B) provider runs the code you funded → TEE attestation or accept trust; (C) inbox spam → ocap addressing, decide early. v0 dodges all Tier3: two owned nodes, no money, caps from day one.

PINNED (grill branch 1+spawn): two identity classes — long-lived roots (cold key + short-lived delegation certs, root compromise = death) vs disposable actor ids (single key, compromise = kill lease + respawn; funding tree is the recovery). spawn(image@digest, payment, intro{parent id, rendezvous, nonce}) → promise{id, rendezvous_hint, lease_handle}; lease_handle ≠ id (kill switch vs address). v0 axiom: child identity trusted because parent trusts purchased compute — allowance-bounded; OCI signing pins WHICH code (digest), TEE attestation later proves it RAN. Chain-registry rule-out logged in exploration-log 2026-08-16.

PINNED (grill branch 3): capability-invocation is the only messaging primitive. ONE data structure system-wide: signed expiring attenuable delegation cert {iss,aud,can,cav,exp,sig} — used for key rotation, membership, and messaging authority. Receiver is root CA of its own attack surface: every valid proof chain starts with a cert the receiver minted. Intro nonce = sole bearer token, exchanged for starter-kit certs at birth. Attenuation = append link, offline, no registration (parent never learns of grandchildren). Public reachability = explicitly minted aud:* facet cert with caveats (postage/rate) = spam economics at point of exposure. Revocation = short expiry + renew facet + lease kill; no lists. Model sentence: identity names you; a message is proof the receiver transitively invited it.

PINNED (grill branch 2): location = self-signed expiring record {iss, reach-me-at, endpoints[], exp} — same cert shape. Primary distribution: piggyback on every message/renew (capability graph = routing table; regular correspondents never look up). Fallback/bootstrap: lighthouse = plain actor with #publish (membership-caveat = joining) + #lookup (privacy dial: aud:* or members-only, default members-only). Domain descriptor = {lighthouse endpoints, lighthouse pubkey, publish-cap} — isomorphic to nebula config triple. Multi-domain attachment = holding publish-caps to multiple lighthouses. Re-landing: publish fresh records first; disposable actors just respawn w/ new id. NAT: relay: endpoints = actors with paid #relay facet (ADR-0006 lesson: relay-by-default). Lighthouses replicable; established links survive lighthouse outage via piggyback.

PINNED (grill branch 5a, frontdoor amendment): well-known frontdoor facet minted by default, revocable (go dark by non-renewal) — publicness default-on, sovereignty at admission time via caveats. Postage condition: fee ≥ processing cost INCLUDING fee verification (one cheap check). Flood becomes revenue. Settlement pluggable: PoW v0, probabilistic tickets (Orchid-style) as money candidate. Stranger-reachability additionally requires a public #lookup somewhere.

PINNED (grill branch 5, complete): protocol ships ZERO economic enforcement — sovereign wallets, tranche funding on the renewal beat, observability; economic blast radius = tranche × detection lag by default. HOWEVER hard bounds are negotiable: offers = capabilities with terms in cav (opaque to protocol core — no chain types in core, ever). Negotiated instruments: paymaster gas sponsorship (solves newborn gas bootstrap), child-OWNED smart account granting parent a bounded guardian role (puppet scheme inverted — hard bound as chosen contract, removable at maturity), payment channels for repeated pairs (regular-correspondent postage settlement; PoW/tickets for strangers). Maturation arc: sponsored+guarded newborn → earning via facets → unguarded independence. Imposed-vs-negotiated is the reconciling principle.

Shareable design doc written: docs/sovereign-actor-protocol.md (v4). Hardened via 3 adversarial cold-reader rounds (fresh pi -p --no-session agent each round, teach-back probes). Round 1: comprehension gaps fixed (terms, seq, bootstrap exception). Round 2 found real design gaps, now addressed in-doc: root compromise = CAPTURE not death (roots never expire); orphan arc (independence = diversified renewable edges); fake-child epistemic damage (wrong answers, not just theft); parent-compromise threat model (open problem #3). Round 3: converged — reviewer's top weaknesses all mapped to doc-acknowledged open problems. Residue = spec-depth items, listed in doc. NOTE for tests: pi -p needs stdin closed (</dev/null) + timeout wrapper or it hangs.

v0 IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: Go, ~2-3k LOC. Packages: cert (the primitive, ~400 LOC, property-test hard), envelope, actor runtime (mailbox/facets/renew/piggyback), lighthouse (~150 LOC — just an actor), spawn (provider iface: k8s Job + docker; Akash later), actorctl CLI. Two cost-collapsing decisions: EIP-191 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON (existing wallet = working root on day one, reuses hub signing code) + nebula mesh as v0 transport (confidentiality/NAT/relay inherited, transport crypto deferred not botched). Milestones M1 certs→M2 two actors on cp1/w1→M3 lighthouse on fly hub + frontdoor/PoW→M4 spawn-as-k8s-Job (v0 complete, Tier-3 dodged)→M5 money on testnet. Not built: DHT, TEE, chain code, store-and-forward.

title: Go config server — device-flow OAuth, single-use identity-bound tokens, SIWE/passkey approval, KMS v2, fly.io
notes:
Use talos machinery libs (configloader/configpatcher) instead of shelling to talosctl — identical patch semantics, static binary, FROM scratch image

OAuth device flow (RFC 8628): kernel args talos.config.oauth.client_id + extra_variable=uuid,mac,serial; endpoints default to config URL + /device/code and /token — colocate in same binary

Tokens: single-use, bound at approval to machine identity (uuid/mac); burned after one config fetch; in-memory pending state OK — Talos restarts flow on failure

Admin approval: SIWE-style sig verify against hardcoded EOA address(es), or passkey. No client_secret (public client, /proc/cmdline). No OIDC, no chain RPC in auth path — EOA only, offline verification. 1-of-2 addresses as break-glass

Secrets: age key as fly secret, decrypt secrets.yaml.age in memory per approved request only; never plaintext at rest

v2: KMS gRPC (siderolabs/kms-client protocol) for disk unseal — per-boot auth + revocation. BLOCKED on decision: per-boot external dependency (on-LAN host vs fly/ISP); need fallback key slot (TPM/passphrase)

Ordering: auth first, THEN fly deployment (current server hands secrets to anyone with a MAC). Consider switching lookup key from mac to ${uuid} (talos.config supports uuid/mac/serial substitution)

Off-ramp: repo/cluster stay vanilla Talos; self-hosted Omni remains viable later if fleet grows. Remaining gap either way: long-lived talosconfig admin cert

Merged /verify into /status: single operator dashboard (unseal + approvals), session gates viewing only, admin-token break-glass login; /verify now redirects, closing the unauthenticated pending-approvals leak

Post-action responses now POST-redirect-GET to /status (in-place render left browser on /unseal; auto-refresh GET 405'd)
